hero.headline: Stuart downtown dock closes Sunday for $3 million renovation project
hero.teaser: Stuart's downtown public dock closes July 6 for a year-long $3 million renovation that will nearly double slip capacity from 18 to 44.
hero.body:
Stuart's downtown public dock will close July 6 for a $3 million renovation project expected to be complete by next Fourth of July. The project, funded by a state grant and transportation impact fees, will expand the dock's capacity from 18 to 44 slips for both motorized and non-motorized vessels. The renovation will include a 7,500 square foot fixed dock, a 1,400 square foot floating dock and a smaller floating platform. More than 1,400 boaters use the dock annually.

Stuart Mayor Sean Reed said the upgrades will prevent storm damage during hurricanes and major storms. During the closure, the city is accommodating businesses that rely on the dock. Tiki Taxi & Cruises, which operates off the dock, will continue running during construction. Austin Kuyrkendall, director of operations for Tiki Taxi & Cruises, said the city is allowing the company to build a gate at the non-floating section of the downtown Stuart dock for boarding passengers. Kuyrkendall said modernizing and expanding the dock will be beneficial for both the city and the business.

cards.headline: DeSantis signs $117.6 billion state budget with $810 million in vetoes
cards.body:
Gov. Ron DeSantis signed a $117.6 billion state budget this week, marking the fourth consecutive year of declining state spending. The term-limited Governor wielded his veto pen to cut nearly $810 million in line-item vetoes, along with blocking another $750 million the Legislature wanted to transfer into the state's rainy-day fund.

DeSantis vetoed items he considered either inappropriate or nice to have, though he noted he was not trying to set a record with his cuts. In 2022, DeSantis vetoed a record-breaking $3.1 billion in state budget funds. The Governor touted the new spending plan as investing billions to accelerate road construction projects, increase teacher pay and make major investments in cancer research. The budget also sets aside $665 million for restoring the Everglades.

Among the notable cuts, DeSantis vetoed $91.5 million intended to increase correctional officers' salaries. Government watchdog Florida TaxWatch had previously urged DeSantis to reject 621 projects worth $830 million in the 2026-27 fiscal year budget, calling them budget turkeys. DeSantis ultimately vetoed 184 out of the 621 appropriations the group wanted eliminated.

The Legislature had proposed the $750 million rainy-day fund transfer to prepare for a new requirement under a proposed constitutional amendment passed by the House last year that would increase the mandated cap on the budget stabilization fund. DeSantis also indicated he would not be formally leading any political committee to campaign for proposed amendments after the Legislature changed his proposals, though he left open the possibility of participating if asked.

cards.headline: Record Fourth of July travel brings heavy traffic and rain to Florida roads
cards.teaser: A record number of Americans traveled this Fourth of July weekend, with South Florida drivers experiencing heavy traffic compounded by rain.
cards.body:
A record number of Americans are traveling this Fourth of July weekend, with South Florida drivers contending with heavy rain and congestion on already-crowded roads. Friday's wet weather created difficult driving conditions on the Florida Turnpike heading south of Orlando. Driver Ed Budd described the conditions as "really beautiful until it starts raining and then everyone forgets how to drive."

AAA estimates 72.2 million Americans will have traveled at least 50 miles from home between Saturday, June 27 and Sunday, July 5, marking an all-time high for the holiday. Of that number, 61.4 million are making the trip by car. Orlando and Miami rank among the top five travel destinations this Independence Day, according to AAA. Drivers reported vastly different experiences on the roads. Carlos Borras and his wife made the round trip between Orlando and Miami on Friday and saw no traffic or accidents. However, driver Fernando Amado said it's been pretty busy, especially with the weather, and noted that Saturday is the day when people are really heading up North. For those still planning to travel, AAA recommends hitting the road after 3 p.m. on Saturday or before 11 a.m. on Sunday to avoid the worst congestion, with the heaviest traffic expected between 10 a.m. Saturday and between noon and 6 p.m. Sunday.

cards.headline: Juno Beach Town Council to decide on fence replacement at JB-7 beach access after condo complaints
cards.teaser: Colony Condos residents say beachgoers are cutting through private property at the JB-7 public walkway since the town removed a fence in 2023. The council will take up the issue during budget discussions on July 15.
cards.body:
Residents at the Colony Condos in Juno Beach are asking the town to replace a fence at the JB-7 public beach access point that was removed in 2023 for safety reasons. Without the fence, only bushes separate the public access path from private property, and residents say people using the walkway are cutting through their land. Lori Hill, a Colony resident, said the problem peaks in summer with people parking in private spots and pushing through bushes with coolers, fishing rods and lawn chairs.

Hill said residents have been calling police to confront trespassers after direct confrontations became hostile. The dispute came before the Juno Beach Town Council at a recent meeting, where a town official noted the town is not obligated to install a fence. Vice Mayor Pro Tem DD Halpern said a lower-cost solution may be worth exploring, suggesting a combination of split rail and shrubs.

The council agreed to take up the fence question as part of its upcoming budget discussions on July 15. Hill said residents are hoping the town will put the fence back up so they can have their landscaping and private parking. Not everyone sees a major issue, with beachgoer Michael House saying he has never noticed anyone hopping the fence or shrubs and that there is plenty of free parking nearby.

cards.headline: Martin County Maritime Response Unit deploys teams for Fourth of July boating weekend
cards.teaser: Lt. Brett Harry said his team will have two boats with medics on standby in north and south Martin County to respond to boating emergencies. Hundreds of boaters are expected on the water this weekend.
cards.body:
Hundreds of boaters are expected to hit Florida's waterways this Fourth of July weekend, prompting Martin County Maritime Response Unit to increase its presence on the water. Lt. Brett Harry with the unit said his team will deploy two boats with medics on standby in north and south Martin County to respond to emergencies throughout the holiday weekend. "We're just out there to mitigate anybody that needs help, whether it's something as simple as a stubbed toe to anything cardiac related, or potential spinal injuries, or anything like that," Harry said.

Among those launching boats Friday at Sandsprit Park in Martin County were Brendan and Ashley Shannon, who were heading out with their young daughter and puppy. The Shannons said safety is top of mind when heading onto the water. Harry urged boaters to do their part by keeping their eyes on the water, having a designated driver, and packing life vests, whistles and flotation devices. "Just have fun and be safe," Harry said.

cards.headline: Martin County School Board fights judge's order to reinstate teacher suspended over Charlie Kirk comments
cards.body:
The Martin County School Board is challenging a judge's recommendation to reinstate Matt Theobald, a social studies teacher at Spectrum Academy since 2009, who was suspended following social media comments about Charlie Kirk. In a Thursday court filing, the school board argued that Administrative Law Judge Jodi-Ann Vanessa Livingstone erred in her recommendation, stating that "numerous findings ... are not based upon competent substantial evidence." According to an investigation report obtained by WPTV, Theobald acknowledged writing comments that labeled Kirk as racist, misogynistic, and a neo-Nazi. He stated the posts were made on his mother's private Facebook page "within a discussion among personal acquaintances" and were not intended for public view. The school board's attorney contends the Facebook post constituted a "serious offense" that justified Theobald's removal.

Administrative Law Judge Livingstone issued an order last month recommending Theobald be reinstated with back pay and benefits. In her ruling, Livingstone cited a recent Florida Fifth District Court of Appeal decision stating that disciplining a teacher for personal Facebook posts made off school grounds, on personal equipment, with no student involvement, violated the teacher's First Amendment rights. The school board retains final authority over whether Theobald returns to his position, with no timeline announced for a decision. After the judge's recommendation, Theobald told WPTV the case raises a larger question about where the line is drawn for teachers speaking outside of school.

cards.headline: Saint Andrew's Scots football targets state title after 10-2 season and district championship
cards.body:
The Saint Andrew's Scots football program is targeting a state title in the 2026 fall season after finishing last year with a 10-2 record and a district championship. Despite their success, a second-round playoff exit has motivated the team to pursue deeper postseason runs. Head football coach Jimmy Robertson emphasized the strength of his senior class, noting that most are four-year players who came through the middle school program. Robertson believes their veteran leadership positions the team to have its best season yet.

The Scots are taking a strategic approach to improvement by scheduling more challenging opponents. Senior Jack Williams stated the program deliberately created a tougher schedule to compete at higher levels and attract new talent. Senior Jack Whelche reinforced this focus, explaining that postseason advancement is the only meaningful measure of success. Whelche noted that an undefeated regular season is irrelevant if the team continues losing in the second round. Senior Edmyer St. Jean described summer workouts as motivation, viewing daily training as an investment in breaking records and achieving positive results when the season begins.

hero.headline: Riviera Beach named only Florida city to win 2026 All-America City Award
hero.teaser: Riviera Beach was one of just 10 communities nationwide to receive the prestigious National Civic League honor. Mayor Douglas Lawson called the recognition a proud moment for the city.
hero.body:
The City of Riviera Beach was named one of just 10 communities in the U.S. to receive the 2026 All-America City Award from the National Civic League, making it the only Florida city selected for the honor this year. The award was announced during the National Civic League conference in Denver, where Riviera Beach leaders presented the city's efforts to strengthen community engagement. Mayor Douglas Lawson called the recognition a proud moment for the city, stating "Little old Riviera Beach is one of the biggest, brightest, shining stars." Lawson said the city earned the award through a long-term effort to revitalize Riviera Beach and improve quality of life for residents.

Riviera Beach's application highlighted several civic participation programs, including the Riviera Beach Youth Council, which helps high school students become involved in civic leadership and advocacy, and the Citizens Leadership Academy, a civic education initiative with a 98% completion rate. The city also highlighted the Neighborhood Reclaim Home Rehabilitation Program, which provides mini-grants to help longtime homeowners make critical repairs. Councilwoman KaShamba Miller-Anderson credited residents for the honor, saying "This award is a tribute to the heart and determination of our residents." She added that winning the award brings back community pride and reinforces the city's positive momentum. The All-America City Award has been presented annually since 1949 and is considered one of the nation's most respected civic honors.

cards.headline: S.D. Spady Elementary in Delray Beach jumps from C to A rating as Palm Beach County schools earn third consecutive A
cards.teaser: The School District of Palm Beach County earned an A rating from the state for the third consecutive year. S.D. Spady Elementary made a dramatic leap from a C rating last year to an A this year.
cards.body:
The School District of Palm Beach County earned an "A" rating from the Florida Department of Education for the third consecutive year, with 143 district-operated schools rated "A" or "B" this year, up from 120 schools the previous year. The district also achieved a record-setting 93.5% graduation rate, with 86% of seniors participating in college-level coursework through Advanced Placement, International Baccalaureate, Cambridge Advanced International Certificate of Education, or Dual Enrollment courses. Additionally, 144 recent graduates earned an associate degree alongside their high school diploma.

S.D. Spady Elementary School in Delray Beach made a dramatic leap from a "C" rating last year to an "A" this year. Principal Rona Tata, who has served 15 years as principal and five years as assistant principal, led the turnaround. The school had an A rating two years ago and narrowly missed a B rating last year by just a few points. Three years ago, staff began modifying the school's early childhood curriculum program, which starts at age 3 and combines with kindergarten. Many of those students are now in third grade and performing at higher levels. The school also fine-tuned its academic approach with last year's theme of "Be the reason you succeed." Spady was one of four district schools to improve from a C to an A rating, along with Dwight D. Eisenhower K-8, Glade View Elementary, and West Gate Elementary.

cards.headline: Peacock House Art Foundation transforms Fort Pierce into artistic destination with global residency program
cards.teaser: The nonprofit organization preserves the Crain Estate and connects local and international artists through its residency program. Visitors can take guided tours every Monday, Wednesday and Friday.
cards.body:
The Peacock House Art Foundation is transforming Fort Pierce into an artistic destination by preserving the historic Crain Estate and connecting local and international artists. The nonprofit honors the legacy of Jaxson and Mary Crain, who built the property. Mr. Crain was a tile worker whose craftsmanship is visible throughout the facility from the ground to the walls to the ceiling. The estate remains 90 percent the way it was when the Crains lived there, including details like the smoking and bourbon room with its man paneling and stained glass leading to a front patio bar. The couple traveled the world nine times, collecting one-of-a-kind items including a gazebo shipped from India. Visitors can take guided tours of the lush gardens and vibrant architecture every Monday, Wednesday, and Friday.

The foundation's artist-in-residency program attracts artists from around the world and offers simple but elegant accommodations on the property. Art director Krystal Masters leads one-on-one classes in the art lab designed for complete beginners. The facility features mediums including sculpting and watercolor, with classes available for children and adults of all skill levels. The Peacock House gets its name from the birds roaming the property for decades. The Crains are believed to have introduced seven peacocks to Fort Pierce in the 1970s. The property now has over 100 peacocks, including a beloved bird named Bob believed to be 60 years old who walks with a limp and receives daily hand-feeding.

cards.headline: Record Fourth of July travel brings heavy traffic and rain to Florida Turnpike south of Orlando
cards.teaser: AAA estimates 72.2 million Americans will have traveled at least 50 miles from home between June 27 and July 5, marking an all-time high. Of that number, 61.4 million are making the trip by car.
cards.body:
A record number of Americans are traveling this Fourth of July weekend, with South Florida drivers facing heavy rain and crowded roads on the Florida Turnpike heading south of Orlando. Friday's wet weather made for a tough start to the holiday weekend. Driver Ed Budd said the conditions were beautiful until the rain started, when "everyone forgets how to drive." AAA estimates 72.2 million Americans will have traveled at least 50 miles from home between Saturday, June 27 and Sunday, July 5, marking an all-time high for the holiday. Of that number, 61.4 million are making the trip by car. Orlando and Miami rank among the top five travel destinations this Independence Day, according to AAA.

Experiences on the road have varied widely. Carlos Borras and his wife made the round trip between Orlando and Miami on Friday and reported smooth sailing with no traffic or accidents. Meanwhile, driver Fernando Amado described a much busier experience, noting that "it's been pretty busy, especially with the weather." For those still planning to travel, AAA recommends hitting the road after 3 p.m. on Saturday or before 11 a.m. on Sunday to avoid the worst congestion. The heaviest traffic is expected between 10 a.m. on Saturday and between noon and 6 p.m. on Sunday.

hero.headline: Martin County School Board fights judge's order to reinstate teacher suspended over Charlie Kirk comments
hero.body:
The Martin County School Board is opposing a judge's recommendation that would bring back a teacher who was suspended following social media posts about political commentator Charlie Kirk. Matt Theobald has taught social studies at Spectrum Academy since 2009. His suspension came after he posted comments on Facebook that characterized Kirk as racist, misogynistic, and a neo-Nazi. The school board filed court documents Thursday arguing that Administrative Law Judge Jodi-Ann Vanessa Livingstone made errors in her ruling and that "numerous findings are not based upon competent substantial evidence." The board's legal team maintains that Theobald's Facebook post represented a serious violation that justified his removal from the classroom.

The judge's recommendation relied heavily on recent legal precedent from Florida's Fifth District Court of Appeal. That ruling established that teachers cannot be disciplined for personal social media posts created outside of work, using personal devices, and without any student involvement, as such action violates First Amendment protections. In her order from last month, Livingstone applied this standard to Theobald's case. She recommended not only that Theobald be reinstated but that he also receive back pay and employee benefits for the time he has been away from his position.

According to an investigation report reviewed by WPTV, Theobald acknowledged that he wrote the comments about Kirk. However, he stated that he posted them on his mother's private Facebook page as part of a conversation with personal friends. He indicated that he did not intend for the posts to reach a wider audience beyond that private circle. This detail about the limited audience and private nature of the forum became significant to the judge's reasoning in recommending his reinstatement.

The final decision on Theobald's employment status rests with the school board, which has not yet indicated when it will rule on the judge's recommendation. Following the judge's order, Theobald discussed with WPTV how his case highlights broader questions about the boundaries of free speech for teachers outside school settings. The dispute raises important questions about what protections teachers have when expressing personal opinions on their own time and platforms, and where school districts can and cannot restrict their employees' speech. As the Martin County School Board considers its next steps, the case continues to highlight tensions between employee rights and school board authority.

Riviera Beach was a first-time winner.

Mayor Douglas Lawson called the recognition a proud moment for the city, saying "Little old Riviera Beach is one of the biggest, brightest, shining stars." Riviera Beach's application highlighted several programs including the Riviera Beach Youth Council, the Citizens Leadership Academy with a 98% completion rate, and the Neighborhood Reclaim Home Rehabilitation Program. Councilwoman KaShamba Miller-Anderson credited residents for the honor, stating "This award is a tribute to the heart and determination of our residents." cards.headline: Port St. Lucie approves land transfer for new Florida Turnpike interchange at Midway Road
cards.teaser: Port St. Lucie City Council approved the first reading of an ordinance to give 7 acres of land to the Florida Department of Transportation for a partial interchange on Florida's Turnpike. The city says the interchange will accommodate growth over the next 20 to 50 years.
cards.body:
Port St. Lucie City Council last month approved the first reading of an ordinance to give 7 acres of land to the Florida Department of Transportation to assist with a partial interchange at the Florida Turnpike. Scott Samples, strategic communications manager for Port St. Lucie, said there is a significant gap between the entrances and exits to the Turnpike currently in the city.

FDOT has been constructing the $95 million Midway Road Widening Project to help with congestion and safety. Crews are currently working on the first phase, widening the road from two lanes to four lanes from Selvitz Road to Jenkins Road. According to the FDOT website, the second widening phase from Jenkins Road to Glades Cut Off Road is still in the design phase with construction anticipated to begin in Summer 2027.

The partial interchange is still in the design phase. The project will also add bike and pedestrian paths along with sidewalks. City council will vote on final approval to give the land at an upcoming meeting.

Guided tours of the lush gardens and vibrant architecture are available every Monday, Wednesday, and Friday. The couple traveled the world nine times, collecting one-of-a-kind items for their Florida estate, including a gazebo shipped from India. The Crains are believed to have introduced peacocks to Fort Pierce in the 1970s. From what the foundation hears, they brought in seven originally, and from those seven there are now over 100. cards.headline: St. Lucie County marine deputies rescue two after boat sinks in Intracoastal Waterway
cards.teaser: Two boaters are safe after their vessel sank in the Intracoastal Waterway on Wednesday. The St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office Marine Unit responded to reports of a small motorized boat taking on water and becoming submerged on July 1.
cards.body:
Two boaters are safe after their vessel sank in the Intracoastal Waterway on Wednesday, thanks to a quick response from marine deputies and the life-saving decision to wear life jackets. The St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office Marine Unit responded to reports of a small motorized boat taking on water and becoming submerged on July 1. Body-worn camera footage captured the rescue as it unfolded.

Both occupants ended up in the water when their boat went down, but deputies say they were wearing life jackets that kept them afloat while help arrived. Marine Unit deputies quickly located the pair in the water and safely brought them aboard their patrol vessel. The boaters were then transported back to the boat ramp without any injuries reported. "This incident serves as an important reminder that wearing a life jacket can save your life," the sheriff's office said in a Facebook post. "We're grateful this call ended safely and proud of the swift response by our Marine Unit deputies who are always ready to answer the call."

cards.headline: Hobe Sound community fundraises for man who lost fiance in deadly home fire
cards.teaser: Misty Dawn White, 46, was found dead Monday after a fire broke out inside her Hobe Sound home. Friends have launched a fundraiser to help her fiance Mark rebuild after the flames destroyed many belongings.
cards.body:
Misty Dawn White, 46, was found dead Monday after a fire broke out inside her and her fiancé's Hobe Sound home. Preliminary findings from the sheriff's office point to an electrical issue as a possible cause. The fire remains under investigation.

Nina Fenn, a friend of White's for eight years, learned of the death through a phone call from White's fiancé, Mark. Friends have since launched a fundraiser to help Mark rebuild after the flames destroyed many of his and White's belongings. Fenn described White as a Christian woman who loved gardening, plants and playing piano. White's birthday was the Fourth of July, meaning she passed just days before turning a year older. Fenn said the loss is compounded by grief Mark has already endured, noting that he lost his one and only child, Jacob, tragically. "She'll always be in our hearts," Fenn said of her friend.

cards.headline: Fourth of July cookout costs up 4% this year, ground beef and buns see biggest increases
cards.teaser: A Fourth of July meal for 10 now costs $73.82, up 4% from a year ago, according to the American Farm Bureau Federation's Summer Cookout Cost Survey. Ground beef is up 5.5% and buns are up 7.7%.
cards.body:
A Fourth of July meal for 10 now costs $73.82, up 4% from a year ago, according to the American Farm Bureau Federation's Summer Cookout Cost Survey. The increase reflects broader inflation pressures on cookout staples. Ground beef prices have risen 5.5%, while buns are up 7.7%. Strawberries, impacted by a Florida frost, have seen the steepest increase at 12.4%. Ice cream prices are also up 5.3% compared to last year.

Not all cookout items have become more expensive. Potato prices are down this year, benefiting those planning to serve potato chips and salad. Corn prices have fluctuated, though locally grown corn from the Glades can provide better value. Budgeting expert Andrea Woroch recommends shopping strategically by comparing prices across stores to find the best deals for specific grocery items. She emphasized that families should focus on reducing food waste, which begins with creating a meal plan.

cards.headline: Stuart downtown dock closes Monday for $3 million renovation, doubling boat slip capacity
cards.body:
Stuart's downtown public dock will close July 6 for a $3 million renovation project expected to be complete by next Fourth of July. The year-long upgrade will nearly double the dock's capacity, expanding from 18 to 44 slips for both motorized and non-motorized vessels. The project, funded by a state grant and transportation impact fees, will include a 7,500 square foot fixed dock, a 1,400 square foot floating dock and a smaller floating platform. Mayor Sean Reed said the upgrades serve a critical purpose beyond capacity expansion, designed to prevent storm damage during hurricanes and major storms. With more than 1,400 boaters using the dock annually, the improvements represent a significant investment in Stuart's waterfront infrastructure.

During the closure, the city is accommodating businesses that depend on the dock. Tiki Taxi & Cruises, which operates water taxi services from the facility, initially had concerns about continuing operations during construction. However, the city approved building a gate at the end of the non-floating section of the dock, allowing the company to board passengers there throughout the renovation. Austin Kuyrkendall, director of operations for Tiki Taxi & Cruises, emphasized the dock's importance to Stuart's identity and economy. "Stuart is not Stuart without the water," Kuyrkendall said. Boat captain Parker Fisher, based in Stuart, expressed support for the project, hoping the renovation would include additional floating docks.

cards.headline: Martin County School Board fights judge's order to reinstate teacher suspended over Charlie Kirk comments
cards.teaser: The Martin County School Board filed court papers Thursday opposing a judge's recommendation to reinstate Matt Theobald, a Spectrum Academy teacher suspended last year after social media comments about Charlie Kirk.
cards.body:
Matt Theobald, a social studies teacher at Spectrum Academy since 2009, was suspended following social media comments that labeled Charlie Kirk as racist, misogynistic and a neo-Nazi. In a Thursday court filing, the Martin County School Board argued that Administrative Law Judge Jodi-Ann Vanessa Livingstone erred in recommending Theobald's reinstatement, saying "numerous findings ... are not based upon competent substantial evidence." The board's attorney contended that Theobald's Facebook post about Kirk was a "serious offense" and that removing him was appropriate.

In an order issued last month, Livingstone cited a recent Florida Fifth District Court of Appeal ruling stating that disciplining a teacher for personal Facebook posts made off school grounds, on personal equipment, with no student involvement, violated the teacher's First Amendment rights. The judge also recommended Theobald be awarded back pay and benefits. According to an investigation report, Theobald admitted writing the comments about Kirk but said they were posted on his mother's private Facebook page "within a discussion among personal acquaintances" and were not intended for public view. The school board retains final authority on whether Theobald returns to his position.

cards.headline: Hobe Sound woman dies in Monday house fire as community raises funds for fiance
cards.teaser: Misty Dawn White, 46, was found dead Monday after a fire broke out inside her Hobe Sound home. Friends have launched a fundraiser to help her fiance Mark rebuild.
cards.body:
Misty Dawn White, 46, died Monday in a fire at her Hobe Sound home. Preliminary findings from the sheriff's office point to an electrical issue as a possible cause. The fire remains under investigation.

Nina Fenn, a friend of White's for eight years, learned of the death through a phone call from White's fiancé Mark. Friends have launched a fundraiser to help Mark rebuild after the flames destroyed many of his and White's belongings. Fenn said the loss is compounded by grief Mark has already endured after losing his only child, Jacob. White was a Christian woman who loved gardening, plants, and playing piano, and was always willing to help others. White's birthday is the Fourth of July, just days after she passed away.

cards.headline: Record Fourth of July travel brings heavy traffic to Florida Turnpike near Orlando
cards.teaser: AAA estimates 72.2 million Americans will have traveled at least 50 miles from home between Saturday, June 27 and Sunday, July 5, with 61.4 million traveling by car.
cards.body:
A record number of Americans are traveling this Fourth of July weekend, with heavy rain adding to driving challenges on already-crowded roads. Friday's wet weather made for difficult conditions on the Florida Turnpike heading south of Orlando. AAA estimates 72.2 million Americans will travel at least 50 miles from home between Saturday, June 27 and Sunday, July 5, marking an all-time high for the holiday. Of that number, 61.4 million are making the trip by car. Orlando and Miami rank among the top five travel destinations this Independence Day, according to AAA.

Experiences on the road varied for drivers Friday. Carlos Borras and his wife made the round trip between Orlando and Miami and reported smooth conditions, saying they saw no traffic or accidents. Driver Fernando Amado described a busier experience, noting that "it's been pretty busy, especially with the weather" and that Saturday appeared to be when people were heading north. For those still planning to travel, AAA recommends hitting the road after 3 p.m. on Saturday or before 11 a.m. on Sunday to avoid the worst congestion. The heaviest traffic is expected between 10 a.m. on Saturday and between noon and 6 p.m. on Sunday.

cards.headline: Breast cancer patient speaks out after insurance denies reconstruction surgery hours before procedure
cards.teaser: Beth Clark, 48, had her insurance deny coverage for breast reconstruction surgery less than 24 hours before it was scheduled, but her surgeon found a way to complete the procedure.
cards.body:
Beth Clark, 48, was diagnosed three months ago with invasive ductal carcinoma, the most common type of breast cancer. She underwent a full double bilateral mastectomy, but less than 24 hours before her scheduled reconstruction surgery, her insurance company, Anthem Blue Cross and Blue Shield, denied coverage for the procedure. According to her denial letter, the surgery involving a surgical mesh called GalaFlex is still considered investigational with insufficient proof that it improves health. Despite the denial, Clark received her reconstruction surgery with the GalaFlex mesh a little more than a week ago, thanks to her plastic surgeon Dr. Alicia Billington.

Dr. Billington uses GalaFlex mesh on most of her breast reconstruction patients and says the product gives her patients the least amount of complications compared to other options. While GalaFlex is FDA-approved for some uses in the body, it is not approved for breast reconstruction and remains an off-label treatment. In a 2023 letter to health care providers, the FDA stated its efficacy and safety for breast cancer patients have not been determined. Anthem responded to Clark's denial by stating the mesh does not currently meet the standards required for coverage by their medical policy without FDA approval. Last year, Cigna became the first and only major insurer to start approving GalaFlex for breast reconstruction.

cards.headline: Saint Andrew's Scots football targets state title after 10-2 season and district championship
cards.body:
The Saint Andrew's Scots football program is targeting a state title in the 2026 fall season after finishing last year with a 10-2 record and a district championship. Despite their success, a second-round playoff exit has motivated the team to pursue deeper postseason runs. Head football coach Jimmy Robertson emphasized the strength of his senior class, noting that most are four-year players who came through the middle school program. Robertson believes their veteran leadership positions the team to have its best season yet.

The Scots are taking a strategic approach to improvement by scheduling more challenging opponents. Senior Jack Williams stated the program deliberately created a tougher schedule to compete at higher levels and attract new talent. Senior Jack Whelche reinforced this focus, explaining that postseason advancement is the only meaningful measure of success. Whelche noted that an undefeated regular season is irrelevant if the team continues losing in the second round. Senior Edmyer St. Jean described summer workouts as motivation, viewing daily training as an investment in breaking records and achieving positive results when the season begins.

hero.headline: Loggerhead Marinelife Center in Juno Beach offers sea turtle nesting programs through September
hero.body:
Loggerhead Marinelife Center in Juno Beach is offering educational and interactive programs during peak sea turtle nesting season through September. Guests can participate in guided Turtle Walks, the Hatchling Discovery Program, Hatchling Releases, Tidal Tots and Plastic Free July Community Action Day. The programs are designed to give visitors an opportunity to learn about sea turtle conservation along one of the world's busiest sea turtle nesting beaches.

The Turtle Walk program allows participants to observe the nesting process while learning about sea turtle biology, conservation and ongoing research efforts. Educational demonstrations may include the use of red-light headlamps, amber lighting, night scopes and research tag scanning equipment. The center's education and research departments work together during nesting season to collect and analyze data related to nesting activity and hatchling success. Sea turtle nesting season in Florida typically runs from March through October. Conservation groups continue encouraging beachgoers to turn off beachfront lighting at night, properly dispose of trash and avoid disturbing nesting turtles or hatchlings. Registration information and program details are available through Loggerhead Marinelife Center.

hero.headline: Florida state parks waive admission fees for America's 250th anniversary weekend
hero.teaser: The Florida Department of Environmental Protection offered free admission to state parks from Friday through Sunday to celebrate Independence Day and the nation's semiquincentennial.
hero.body:
The Florida Department of Environmental Protection waived admission fees from Friday, July 3, 2026, through Sunday, July 5, 2026, at Florida State Parks to celebrate America's 250th anniversary. DEP Secretary Alexis A. invited all Floridians, their friends and family to enjoy the outdoors, make new memories and support the state's public lands during the significant milestone in the nation's history.

Florida's state parks offer hiking, camping, wildlife viewing, swimming, paddling and horseback riding, along with historic sites including forts, battlefields, archaeological sites and other landmarks. The Florida State Park system is the only four-time winner of the NRPA's National Gold Medal Award. Over the last fiscal year, Florida State Parks saw more than 28 million visitors, generating an estimated $3.6 billion in statewide economic impact. The free admission applied to day use only and excluded Ellie Schiller Homosassa Springs Wildlife State Park, Skyway Fishing Pier State Park and Weeki Wachee Springs State Park. All other fees, including overnight accommodations, special events, concessions and rentals, remained in effect.

cards.headline: DeSantis signs $117.6 billion state budget with $810 million in vetoes
cards.body:
Gov. Ron DeSantis signed a $117.6 billion state budget this week, marking the fourth consecutive year of declining state spending. The term-limited Governor wielded his veto pen to cut nearly $810 million in line-item vetoes, along with blocking another $750 million the Legislature wanted to transfer into the state's rainy-day fund.

DeSantis vetoed items he considered either inappropriate or nice to have, though he noted he was not trying to set a record with his cuts. In 2022, DeSantis vetoed a record-breaking $3.1 billion in state budget funds. The Governor touted the new spending plan as investing billions to accelerate road construction projects, increase teacher pay and make major investments in cancer research. The budget also sets aside $665 million for restoring the Everglades.

Among the notable cuts, DeSantis vetoed $91.5 million intended to increase correctional officers' salaries. Government watchdog Florida TaxWatch had previously urged DeSantis to reject 621 projects worth $830 million in the 2026-27 fiscal year budget, calling them budget turkeys. DeSantis ultimately vetoed 184 out of the 621 appropriations the group wanted eliminated.

The Legislature had proposed the $750 million rainy-day fund transfer to prepare for a new requirement under a proposed constitutional amendment passed by the House last year that would increase the mandated cap on the budget stabilization fund. DeSantis also indicated he would not be formally leading any political committee to campaign for proposed amendments after the Legislature changed his proposals, though he left open the possibility of participating if asked.

cards.headline: Southwest Florida celebrates America's 250th with fireworks, parades and drone shows
cards.teaser: Communities from Sarasota to Fort Myers Beach marked the semiquincentennial with waterfront celebrations, Fourth of July parades and fireworks displays across the region.
cards.body:
Southwest Florida hosted Fourth of July weekend celebrations across multiple communities to mark America's 250th birthday. Sarasota's bayfront hosted an America250 fireworks display beginning at 9 p.m., while Waterside Place in Lakewood Ranch at 1560 Lakefront Drive featured circus acts, carnival games, a kids zone and a drone show over the water at 9 p.m. Siesta Beach held its 35th annual community fireworks show from 8 to 9:30 p.m., funded entirely by local residents, businesses and community supporters.

Bradenton and Palmetto celebrated together with festivities on both sides of the Manatee River, including activities along the Bradenton Riverwalk, Rossi Park, Old Main Street and Palmetto's Riverside Park. Palmetto's 15th annual Fourth Fest featured 14 food trucks, 20 artisan and community vendors, a "Lil Firecrackers" kids zone and live music, with fireworks visible from both sides of the river. Venice held a patriotic parade through Historic Downtown Venice beginning at 9:30 a.m., with fireworks at the South Jetty scheduled between 9 and 9:15 p.m. and contingency plans to reschedule to July 5 in case of inclement weather. Fort Myers Beach kicked off celebrations with a parade starting at 10 a.m. at Bay Oaks Recreation Center, followed by fireworks launched from a barge near Times Square around 9 p.m., with Matanzas Pass Bridge closing from around 8:30 to 11:30 p.m.

cards.headline: Marion County stages four synchronized fireworks displays for America's 250th
cards.teaser: Ocala and Marion County celebrated the semiquincentennial with four synchronized fireworks shows, parades and free aquatic activities across the county.
cards.body:
Marion County is staging four synchronized fireworks displays on July 4 to commemorate America's 250th anniversary under the Marion Celebrates 250 banner. Each display begins at 5 p.m. with live entertainment, food vendors and family activities before fireworks at 9 p.m. The four locations are Veterans Memorial Park in Ocala, Wrigley Fields in Citra, Dunnellon High School and the Belleview Sportsplex in Belleview.

The city of Ocala is hosting Fourth in the Park at Tuscawilla Park starting at 10 a.m., a free celebration featuring live music, food trucks, a kids zone and games. Country singer-songwriter Emma Forgette performs from 10 to 11:30 a.m., followed by Nashville recording artist Cliff Dorsey from noon to 2 p.m. The city is also opening its aquatic fun centers, splash pads and Discovery Center for free patriotic pool parties and activities. The Patriot Parade will kick off at Southeast 16th Avenue, head up Silver Springs Boulevard and wrap up near Southeast 25th Avenue, with veteran groups, local businesses and community organizations marching in the early evening. Marion County is promoting the Explore Your Freedom Here theme for summer visitors, highlighting crystal-clear springs, trails, the World Equestrian Center and locally owned restaurants and breweries.

cards.headline: North Port celebrates Independence Day at CoolToday Park
cards.teaser: North Port's Freedom Festival at CoolToday Park featured patriotic entertainment, live music and fireworks to commemorate the nation's 250th anniversary.
cards.body:
North Port will celebrate America's 250th birthday at CoolToday Park with the Freedom Festival: Cheers to 250 Years event running from 6 to 9:30 p.m. The celebration will feature patriotic entertainment, family activities, food vendors and live music. Fireworks are scheduled for 9 p.m., conditions permitting, at the venue on Villages Parkway.

The event is part of a broader Fourth of July weekend celebration across Southwest Florida, with festivities planned throughout the region including Sarasota, Manatee County, Venice and Fort Myers Beach. Communities are marking America's semiquincentennial, which commemorates 250 years since the Declaration of Independence.

cards.headline: Fort Myers hosts concert and combined fireworks-drone show for America's 250th

The Fort Myers event is part of a broader observance of America's 250th birthday across the region. From Sarasota's bayfront to Fort Myers Beach, communities are hosting parades, fireworks shows and drone displays throughout the Fourth of July weekend. Attendees planning to visit the Fort Myers celebration should check fortmyers.gov for the latest updates, as many fireworks shows scheduled near waterfronts and beach areas may experience weather delays.

cards.teaser: Longboat Key celebrated Independence Day with the Shortest Parade in America, a rededication of Bicentennial Park and a hot dog costume contest.
cards.body:
Longboat Key will host the Longboat Key Freedom Fest at Bicentennial Park, 2730 Gulf of Mexico Drive, featuring the "Shortest Parade in America," a rededication of Bicentennial Park and the Hot Diggity Dog costume contest. The St. Regis Longboat Key Resort will host an elevated evening oceanfront BBQ dinner and fireworks display at 1601 Gulf of Mexico Drive in Longboat Key.

These celebrations are part of Southwest Florida's broader Fourth of July weekend festivities marking America's 250th birthday. Communities across the region, including Sarasota, Manatee County, Venice, North Port and Fort Myers Beach, are hosting patriotic events and entertainment to commemorate the semiquincentennial and Independence Day.

AAA estimates 72.2 million Americans will have traveled at least 50 miles from home between Saturday, June 27 and Sunday, July 5, marking an all-time high for the holiday. Of that number, 61.4 million are making the trip by car. Orlando and Miami rank among the top five travel destinations this Independence Day, according to AAA. Drivers reported vastly different experiences on the roads. Carlos Borras and his wife made the round trip between Orlando and Miami on Friday and saw no traffic or accidents. hero.headline: Peacock House Art Foundation preserves historic Crain Estate in Fort Pierce
hero.body:
The Peacock House Art Foundation is establishing Fort Pierce as an artistic destination by preserving the historic Crain Estate in the Peacock Arts District. This non-profit organization maintains the legacy of Jaxson and Mary Crain, the property's original owners. Jaxson Crain worked as a tile worker, and evidence of his skilled craftsmanship covers the entire facility, visible on floors, walls, and ceilings throughout. Guided tours of the gardens and distinctive architecture are available every Monday, Wednesday, and Friday. The house retains much of its original character from the Crain era, including a smoking and bourbon room with wood paneling, masculine-toned bathroom fixtures, and pre-stained glass windows that open to a front patio bar. During their travels around the world nine times, the Crains collected distinctive pieces for their Florida home, including a gazebo shipped from India that features small peacocks in its design. The foundation has deliberately chosen to preserve the estate's authentic character rather than commercialize it, keeping the property approximately 90 percent as it was during the Crains' residency.

The property's name comes from the peacocks that have inhabited it for decades. The Crains are believed to have introduced peacocks to Fort Pierce during the 1970s, initially bringing seven birds to the estate. That original flock has since grown to over 100 peacocks. Among them is Bob, a celebrated bird estimated to be 60 years old and recognizable by his distinctive limp. Bob has become something of a celebrity, living inside the house with his own feeding bowls and receiving hand-feedings daily. For visitors, particularly children, seeing peacocks eat from their hands creates memorable experiences. Interestingly, the Crains once kept monkeys on the property as well, with one story recounting how Jaxson Crain brought a baby monkey back from South America in his pocket.

The foundation operates an artist-in-residency program that draws creative professionals from around the world. The program provides simple yet elegant accommodations on the property for visiting artists. The art lab offers classes for both children and adults regardless of experience level. Art director Krystal Masters teaches one-on-one sessions specifically designed for beginners, allowing students to arrive with no artistic background and leave with a completed piece. The lab provides various mediums and projects, including sculpting and watercolor painting. One workshop offered is called "paint your pet in watercolor and rainbow," which combines creative instruction with popular subjects.

For Masters, art serves a therapeutic purpose beyond simple creativity. She emphasizes that classes help people destress and leave feeling fulfilled, disconnected from their phones. Students working with her report experiencing genuine satisfaction from their artistic accomplishments, with Masters noting that her work inspires her through witnessing the positive impact on her students.

"Really beautiful until it starts raining and then everyone forgets how to drive," driver Ed Budd said. Despite the conditions, some drivers managed the journey smoothly. Driver Jim Macfawn commented on the scale of travel this year, saying "It sounds like a lot. I'm surprised people can afford all the gas."

AAA estimates 72.2 million Americans will travel at least 50 miles from home between Saturday, June 27 and Sunday, July 5, marking an all-time high for the holiday. Of that number, 61.4 million are making the trip by car. Orlando and Miami rank among the top five travel destinations this Independence Day, according to AAA. Experiences varied among drivers: Carlos Borras and his wife made the round trip between Orlando and Miami on Friday and reported no traffic or accidents, while driver Fernando Amado described busy conditions, noting "It's been pretty busy, especially with the weather." AAA recommends hitting the road after 3 p.m. on Saturday or before 11 a.m. on Sunday to avoid the worst congestion, with the heaviest traffic expected between 10 a.m. and noon on Saturday and between noon and 6 p.m. on Sunday.
